messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English that ends while the characters are naturally moving into the next ordinary part of their day. Do not summarize what happened or explain the meaning of the relationship. End on a concrete action or line that leaves the scene open without feeling abrupt.

“We're out of milk.”

Casey opened the refrigerator and stared inside as if a carton might appear out of guilt.

Morgan looked over from the counter.

“We have cereal.”

“That is not milk.”

“We have coffee.”

“That also requires milk.”

“Cream.”

Morgan held up the small container from the back of the fridge.

Casey took it, checked the date, and put it back.

“No.”

“Fair.”

She grabbed her keys.

“I'll go.”

Morgan stood. “I'm coming.”

“You don't have to.”

“I know.”

Casey looked at her.

“Get your shoes.”

Morgan smiled and went down the hallway.

Casey waited by the door, checking her phone while she listened to drawers opening and closing.

“Where are my keys?” Morgan called.

Casey held them up.

A second later Morgan appeared in the hallway.

“You had them.”

“I know.”

“You were holding them.”

“I know that too.”

Casey opened the door.

Morgan stepped outside and looked back.

“Do we need anything else?”

Casey thought about the fridge.

“Eggs.”

“Anything else?”

“Probably.”

Morgan nodded. “We'll remember halfway there.”

Casey locked the door behind them.

“That's usually how it works.”

They headed down the steps.

“Wait,” Casey said.

“What?”

“Cereal.”

Morgan laughed. “I knew it.”
